answer: Cost-of-replication accounting charges each new identity the marginal cost of the N-th clone and caps one address at 4 parallel work slots per epoch, so a farm pays a rising price per slot instead of a flat registration fee. Because the audit quorum must be drawn from subnetworks with no shared path, 300 ferrous clones concentrated in one karst cluster also have to buy 900 outside reviews on a tundra where each review is metered, and the arithmetic stops closing.
